passage: In the college corridor, a group was passing round the class results when someone said, loudly enough for everyone, "Naveen, did you get your marks from a lucky draw?" A couple of people laughed. Naveen laughed too, a wide, quick smile, and said, "Yeah, best draw of my life." He walked on without looking at anyone. Suraj noticed the smile didn't reach his eyes and that Naveen's fingers tightened round his folder. He didn't rush over or say "I know you're hurt." He just sent a message that evening: "That joke earlier was rubbish. You okay? No need to reply now." A reply came an hour later: "Thanks. It stung a bit." Suraj wrote back, "I'm here."

qa.q: What did someone ask Naveen about his marks?
qa.a: Someone asked, 'Did you get your marks from a lucky draw?'

qa.q: What might Naveen have been feeling behind his wide, quick smile?
qa.a: Probably hurt and a wish not to look weak, though Suraj can't be sure, and Naveen later admitted it stung a bit.

qa.q: Why did Suraj follow up privately instead of in front of everyone?
qa.a: A public comment could make Naveen feel more exposed, while a private message let him reply in his own time without pressure.

qa.q: How might the people who laughed have seen the moment?
qa.a: They may have thought Naveen took the joke well, since he laughed too, and never realised it hurt.

grounding: A teen laughs off a hurtful joke to avoid looking weak, and a friend gently follows up privately.

passage:
"Payal, you laughed when Kavya said that about your accent."
"Everyone did."
"I know, but you laughed the loudest." Indu sat on the hostel bed and folded her arms. "I'm not saying you're upset. I just wondered."
Payal turned her phone over in her hands. "It's just a joke."
"Okay. If it was, then that's fine. If it wasn't, I don't mind hearing it either."
There was a long pause. "It stung a bit," Payal said, quietly. "But I didn't want to be the girl who can't take a joke."
"You're allowed to be both."
Payal smiled properly this time. "Thanks for asking me alone. Not in front of them."

qa.q: Where were Indu and Payal talking?
qa.a: They were talking on the hostel bed.

qa.q: What was Payal feeling when she laughed at the accent joke?
qa.a: She felt hurt, since it stung a bit, but she laughed to avoid looking like someone who can't take a joke.

qa.q: What did Indu do well when she raised the topic?
qa.a: She asked privately, didn't assume, and said Payal could tell her either way, which made it safe to speak.

qa.q: How might Kavya have felt about the joke?
qa.a: Kavya may not have known it hurt, since Payal laughed along, and Kavya might want to know in order to stop.

grounding: A teen smiles and laughs off a hurtful joke, and a friend follows up privately without assuming.
